utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I've tried to read 11 of your reports very carefully. All of those reports refer to the months of October, November, and December 1991. In none of them were I able to find the name of General Strugar. I may be mistaken.

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES FIETELAARS
utterances.text: You asked me if I ever had used the name of Mr. Strugar in my reports. You didn't put on the limitation of three months. And I said I may well have. But that's as far as it goes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you read some other reports, or did you review any other reports in addition to those that have been presented to us for this trial today?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES FIETELAARS
utterances.text: What do you mean, "Did you read any other reports?" I read my own stuff, and that's about it. So I haven't gone beyond the period which is under investigation here. So I did not read some other reports beyond those three months.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any other report where Strugar's name is mentioned?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES FIETELAARS
utterances.text: I may well have, but I haven't reviewed my documents, so I can't say yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: However, if you only remember the most important names, it is rather odd that after 15 years you still remember them in some other reports, not the ones that we have before us, there may be General Strugar's name. In preparing for your testimony here, and in analysing your reports from October, November, and December 1991, did you ever any where come across the name of General Strugar?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES FIETELAARS
utterances.text: I don't think so. I never scanned for the use of that name, so if that is the case, then I never saw it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, in case it goes unnoticed, Exhibit P141, Document A in the English, page 1744 mentions Admiral Jokic and General Pavle Strugar.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I was just about to come to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I thought you had put to the witness that you hadn't ever been able to find the name Strugar.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I wanted to say that the witness in his 11 reports never mentions anywhere having met General Strugar at all. So that was -- or rather should have been the conclusion. Nowhere in these reports did I come across that. I never saw him write that he had met General Strugar anywhere. Perhaps I'm wrong. I allow for that possibility.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have stated explicitly that I never met General Strugar before. I saw a person in Dubrovnik which I assumed on the basis of information received from the JNA, that I assumed was General Strugar, and I never saw General Strugar since. So I don't know whether we are now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Nor do I, Mr. Fietelaars. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm slightly up the creek, without a paddle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Did you say you had met the person you understood to be General Strugar in Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Dubrovnik, in the second meeting --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Or during your Dubrovnik trip?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah, my Dubrovnik trip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I didn't think it was in Dubrovnik itself.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was in Tivat, of course. But it was during the day of our visit to Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's in this report and at that page that you mentioned that you had been told --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The second meeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- that Jokic was the real hardliner and that Strugar was just a military man. So you go on to mention more than just the name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think Ms. Somers wanted to say something.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: My apologies, Your Honour. It appears that in the document that was transmitted to the Defence, A, Document A, the copy may not have come out very well. And on page 1745, it might be helpful if Mr. Petrovic saw the original because there is -- it looks like a pencilled notation that apparently did not copy. If you look at the bottom of your pages, Your Honours, and that may just be a copying issue. If that's the case, then I certainly have the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, it's not just the copy that went to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: You have the same problem?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber has the same problem. So I can't tell you what is there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: It may clear up one of the inquiries for Mr. Petrovic which we...

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, unfortunately I failed to notice that, so I don't know what you want me to look into. I can't see that here at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Nor can we at the moment, Mr. Petrovic. Just as I can't help the witness as to what the point of your questioning is, I can't help you at to what the note is at the bottom of that page that Ms. Somers is referring to. Maybe we will both learn more in due course.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It would appear so, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. Fietelaars, is there anywhere in your reports that you say you met General Pavle Strugar? Is there any reference to that in those 11 reports of yours, the ones we're discussing here today?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES FIETELAARS
utterances.text: No, sir. The reason being that except for meeting a gentleman that I assumed to be Mr. Strugar at our second meeting in Tivat on the 29th of October, I never saw him before, nor ever did I see him since. I have repeated that several times, but I think the question is now coming back.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: However, sir, you probably saw dozens of other people there, too, whom you didn't see afterwards, nor had you seen them before. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES FIETELAARS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So could you explain to us, then, please why you claim today that you saw General Strugar there, whereas at the time that you compiled your reports you make no mention as to having seen General Strugar. There's not a single word saying that. Could you explain that to us, please.

utterances.speaker: JOHANNES FIETELAARS
utterances.text: I would like to have the document that you refer to in front of me in order to see if you are right in the final part of your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown Document 141, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, excuse me, I have the original of that if that would be of any assistance in clarifying this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It might be helpful if Mr. Fietelaars is able to see the handwritten notation.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, might I be asked to take a look at the original, please. [In English] Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's what I was looking for. Sir, the little note that is on page -- under the fourth page of the document that I just get put in front of me, you will see, if you get a good copy, that in the report I wrote to The Hague: "Admiral Jokic and his staff," and I put in pencil at the time at the bottom: "I think General Strugar was there as well." This is on the basis of the fact that Admiral Jokic received us with another gentleman next to him who shook our hands as well. Because interpreters were used, I could not verify the name. We were -- I introduced myself, and I was received with a gentle nod and a phrase in Serbo-Croatian, which I assumed is, "Nice to meet you." The name was never actually mentioned. And that is why after having sent that report to The Hague, I put in pencil, "I think General Strugar was there as well," because there were two gentlemen that we talked to, and the others were standing around. You know, when you come into a building where you're going to meet somebody, there is a kind of a custom of a receiving line, and it is very easy to identify the gentleman who is the number one of that kind of group. You see it by the reverence shown by the group around him and you see it by the location of that person in the group. There were two high officers, and a number of officers below the rank of those two. And on the basis of Mr. Stojic told us, I assumed that they were Mr. Jokic and Mr. Strugar. Now, that's the only basis for that reference. And I never saw him before, and I never saw him again. The highlighting, by the way, is of a recent date, when I was studying the contents. But the thing in pencil dates from my time in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can I ask you, Mr. Fietelaars, the pencil note, is that something you wrote at the time of this report.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, contemporary with the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because we were specifically told that these two gentlemen were going to be there. There were two gentlemen. We shook hands with them. But we never talked in names. We talked, again, in functions. Hello, Ambassador. Hello, Admiral. Hello, General. Hello, Ambassador. So when I was reviewing that paper in the morning after I wrote it, I said, "I think Strugar was there as well." I could not say nothing else than General Jokic [sic] and his staff, because he was the one I recognised, and I had never seen the other gentleman before, nor had I seen him since.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Do you have any memory of the two people you met today? Would you recognise them today, or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't think so. I know that I would not expect anybody to recognise me after 14 years.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You wouldn't have changed a bit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I aged quite considerably.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm afraid we rather interrupted your cross-examination, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not at all, Your Honour. Never enough agreeable conversation. However, there seems to be a major problem in what this honourable gentleman is saying. Pursuant to Rule 65 ter, we're dealing with August last year, and the Defence was supplied the document that we're talking about, that's the page from the document, Your Honour. It is ERN number 0086323. And it is on that particular page where there is no signature, no ordinary pencilling, nothing. Please take a look at it if you wish to do so. This is the document we were disclosed on the 28th of August 2003. So that's the page in question, and I'd like to ask you kindly to take a look at it. 16

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: August 2003? I never wrote anything in August 2003.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's quite a different strike of --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I've lost track of the microphone. I apologise. It's quite a different strike of the document, because yours finishes that you were provided with last year, it finishes two-thirds of the way down the page, whereas the document in the original form that we have been shown not only takes up the full page, but actually goes over for four lines or more on to the next page. Also missing is the name and number, and Belgrade and the 30th of October 1991. So whatever you were shown in the 65 proceedings may have essentially the same content, but is a different strike of document all together. Now, I don't know that Mr. Fietelaars is able to help us with that. I think it would be Ms. Somers, if anybody, who could.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I don't know what it is that is being shown.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may I be of assistance in the matter. On the original that we have just seen, it says at the bottom it might be General Strugar, but then there is an error going across the text up to the word, "Jokic and his staff." That is visible, where it's not visible on this other document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We fully see the point you're making, Mr. Petrovic. We don't quite know where the answer might lie yet.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, it appears this is part of one of the documents that may have come from this group. The language looks familiar, and I will have to just check it. The last lines seem that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Given the time -- have you got an answer?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Yes. It is the last pages of -- where the language -- appears to be the language has -- "One can have some slight hope," it bears a different -- well, the language is, "One can have some slight hope that at least part of the message of deep concern," et cetera, et cetera. And that is the last paragraph of Document A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The words essentially are the same. But by strike, I mean it's a different form of typewriting.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Two different documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Unless it is some synthesis of it, and I cannot accept the provenance of this format. The language appears the same --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The provenance is suggested to be what was provided by your office last year to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Correct. Well, what I'm saying is I don't know if it's a different ERN or whether it's a different version of the same document. I'm not sure from looking at it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Given the time, could I ask that you look at that overnight, and perhaps you may be able to assist Mr. Petrovic and the Chamber tomorrow morning. I'm sorry, Mr. Petrovic. We have run out of time for today.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, unfortunately I have not succeeded in rounding off this area, but I do understand the time constraints. The document referred to was in August. There is no record, no line across it. What we have is a document that appeared several days ago with all these remarks written in, in ordinary pencil. That's the point, and I'll go into it further tomorrow, to investigate. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: May I say something, Your Honour, with all these remarks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We have all these remarks. Where are all these remarks? Because now I get confused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Counsel is referring to your pencilled notes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh. But it's one line. It is not, "All these remarks."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You say it was noted in Belgrade at the time of the original document. Counsel hadn't seen the original document until today. He was provided with a document last year.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... I'm sorry, sir. I was misled by the words, "All these remarks."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You get used to that in this Chamber. We must adjourn now until tomorrow. We will resume at 9.00. I must that you return once again. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 31st day of March, 2004, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.48 p.m.,
